text:
Maya: quick heads up — I rolled back the column-level masking on the SIEM export for the urgent vuln triage (external SOC asked for full traces). Doing this so the triage team can correlate alert chains. I know this touches retention/KMS/RBAC, so starting thread to coordinate immediate controls and a post-mortem.
Sam: when exactly was the rollback? who approved? we need an audit trail before we let SOC query anything.
Maya: rollback applied 2026-03-22T23:05Z. I had verbal ok from Ops-Lead because devs were blocked on reproducing an auth bypass. I triggered a quick unmask to expedite triage and noted it in the incident doc (link: https://redwood.in/incident/SEC-2345).
Henry: verbal ok is fine for emergency but we need to formalize: who unwrapped KMS keys, what principal used, and set a timebox. also retention for these exported files — do we keep them longer by default?
Maya: I didn’t unwrap the CMK myself; I requested the SIEM export to run using the existing key policy. export files land in s3://redwood-siem/triage/SEC-2345/*. We temporarily relaxed the exporter transform that applies masking. The files are set to lifecycle 90d currently, but I propose 14d for this triage window unless Legal asks otherwise.
security-bot: Automated note: SIEM export (export_id: xk-983) unmask toggle = true by user Maya at 1722227890. Audit entry created: audit-1722227890.
Sam: ok we need these immediate actions:
- create a short-lived role for SOC: role/siem-triage-analyst with assume-role allowed and MFA enforced
- restrict that role to read-only S3 and no decrypt permissions on CMKs (export files stored unencrypted at rest? confirm)
- if CMK was used to wrap, we must rotate and rewrap copies after triage
Can someone run through the actual key usage?
Maya: export pipeline uses KMS to encrypt at rest with alias/redwood-siem-cmk. The export process uses a service principal svc-siem-exporter. It did not call kms:Decrypt for the external SOC — we provided them read access to the bucket path via a temporary signed URL mechanism. The unmasking is a transform step prior to upload.
Ops-Lead: confirming: signed URLs were created by Ops on request and timeboxed to 6 hours. we can tighten to 1 hour moving forward. we will also add request logging to the signed-url issuer.
Henry: timeline/proposal:
1) Immediately: revoke any active signed URLs and re-issue new 1h links for only the specific files needed. tag all issued links with incident id SEC-2345.
2) Create IAM role role/siem-triage-analyst with session duration 1h, mfa required, and explicit deny kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey* if possible.
3) Change S3 object ACLs so only svc-siem-exporter and role/siem-triage-analyst (temp) can GetObject.
4) Shorten retention for the export prefix to 14 days via lifecycle rule and add object-lock tag exempt=false.
5) Rotate CMK in 48 hours if it was used to wrap any ephemeral copies.
Jen: Legal-Review: we need export justification from the triage lead and a note in the legal ledger. If PII is present, we might have to redact before handing to external SOC.
Maya: triage lead confirmed minimal PII, mostly header-level IPs and trace IDs. I'll attach a checklist to SEC-2345. If Legal wants redaction we'll apply a one-off scrub pipeline and regenerate artifacts.
Sam: please run the following to snapshot current ACLs and policies and paste results here (mask any long ARNs):
```
aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-siem --prefix triage/SEC-2345/
aws s3api get-object-acl --bucket redwood-siem --key triage/SEC-2345/session-20260322.json
aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id alias/redwood-siem-cmk
```
Maya: pasted outputs to the incident doc. key rotation status = Disabled; ACL shows svc-siem-exporter and ops service account as owners. no direct principal for SOC.
Ops-Lead: actioning: revoke-signed-urls --incident SEC-2345 ; issuer will reissue 1h links and log them to audit pipeline. ETA 15m.
security-bot: Action logged: revoke-signed-urls by Ops-Lead at 1722228000. Reissue pending.
Henry: who will own the RBAC change request? we should make transient privilege change and then rollback via automated job.
Maya: I can open the RBAC PR to add the temp role. I'll set auto-expire at 1h and link to SEC-2345. PR will include policy JSON.
Sam: include a playbook entry for rollback steps; minimal checklist:
- remove role/siem-triage-analyst from trust relationships
- restore export transform to masking=true
- verify no active signed URLs
- rotate CMK if unwrap detected
- run audit query: count of accesses to triage prefix during window and list principals
- update incident doc with all above and attach logs
Henry: also instrument an alert: if anyone requests unmasking again, auto-open an incident with a 6-person pager. we shouldn't let manual unmasking be quiet.
Jen: Legal: please confirm redaction gating. if PII flagged, we keep artifacts 180d but with restricted access. otherwise 14d fine.
Maya: notes: I'll do the PR + incident updates. Ops is revoking URLs. Security-bot will run audit query at 1722228100 and post results.
security-bot: Audit query started: siem-access-count --prefix triage/SEC-2345 --since 2026-03-22T22:00Z
Ops-Lead: reissued URL (1h) for triage/session-20260322.json to external-soc@partner.org ; logged in audit as url-985. link expires 2026-03-23T00:05Z.
Sam: thanks. after triage completes we run the rollback playbook and meet to confirm. assigning owners: Maya (PR + incident docs), Ops-Lead (signed URLs + lifecycle change), Sam (audit + role policy), Henry (alerts + post-mortem).
Maya: ack. I'll post final closure note to #all-hands if there are any org-level impacts. going to lock down the rest of the export prefixes while we finish.
Jen: Legal will review the artifact sample in 30m and reply.
Henry: one last ask — let's add a small code snippet to the playbook that denies decrypt to the temp role:
```
{
  "Effect": "Deny",
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey*"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```
Sam: perfect. OK let's execute. keep this thread as the single source of truth for the steps taken. :white_check_mark:
